nodes.name: Eu-doped Cu₂O synthesis
nodes.procedure: Low-doping Eu/Cu₂O (LD-Eu/Cu₂O) and high-doping Eu/Cu₂O (HD-Eu/Cu₂O) were prepared by a simple liquid-phase reduction using ascorbic acid (Figure 1a). Ascorbic acid was selected as a mild reductant to facilitate the constrained reduction of Cu²⁺ to Cu⁺ for the formation of phase-pure Cu₂O. The Eu contents in LD-Eu/Cu₂O and HD-Eu/Cu₂O were determined to be 0.16 atom % and 14.30 atom %, respectively, by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (Table S1).
nodes.source_text: 2.1. Synthesis and Physical Characterizations. Low-doping Eu/Cu₂O (LD-Eu/Cu₂O) and high-doping Eu/Cu₂O (HD-Eu/Cu₂O) were prepared by a simple liquid-phase reduction using ascorbic acid (Figure 1a).

nodes.name: Chemical reduction to pure Cu
nodes.procedure: A pure Cu sample was further prepared via the chemical reduction by NaBH₄ in the liquid phase.
nodes.source_text: To determine the real active phase, a pure Cu sample was further prepared via the chemical reduction by NaBH₄ in the liquid phase (Figure S24a).

nodes.characterization_summary: Eu contents determined to be 0.16 atom% in LD-Eu/Cu₂O and 14.30 atom% in HD-Eu/Cu₂O.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Eu contents in LD-Eu/Cu₂O and HD-Eu/Cu₂O were determined to be 0.16 atom % and 14.30 atom %, respectively, by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: Diffraction patterns of LD-Eu/Cu₂O and HD-Eu/Cu₂O match standard Cu₂O (PDF 05-0667) with (111) peak shift to lower angle indicating lattice expansion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 1b, the diffraction patterns of LD-Eu/Cu₂O and HD-Eu/Cu₂O matched well with standard Cu₂O (PDF 05-0667) without the detected Eu phases.

nodes.characterization_summary: Eu/Cu₂O samples retain nanocube morphology of ~50 nm after Eu introduction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pure Cu₂O shows a well-defined cubic morphology with a size of ca. 50 nm (Figure S2). After the introduction of Eu, the Eu/Cu₂O samples still retained the structural integrity of the nanocubes (Figure S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform distribution of Cu, Eu, and O elements confirmed in LD-Eu/Cu₂O and HD-Eu/Cu₂O.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping images reveal the uniform distribution of the Cu, Eu, and O elements on LD-Eu/Cu₂O and HD-Eu/Cu₂O

nodes.characterization_summary: Bright spots identified as atomic Eu sites in LD-Eu/Cu₂O and HD-Eu/Cu₂O lattice.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To clarify the atomic distribution of Eu, aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC-HAADF-STEM) was used (Figure 1d-f).

nodes.characterization_summary: Clear Eu site signals observed, stronger in HD-Eu/Cu₂O due to higher Eu loading.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To further capture the elemental distribution, electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) was performed on both LD-Eu/Cu₂O and HD-Eu/Cu₂O (Figure 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu 2p₃/₂ at 932.2 eV and 2p₁/₂ at 952.2 eV for Cu⁺ in Cu₂O; negative shifts in LD-Eu/Cu₂O and HD-Eu/Cu₂O; Cu⁰/Cu⁺ ratios 63.0% (LD) and 85.6% (HD); Eu 3d shows Eu³⁺ (1134.5, 1164.5 eV) and Eu²⁺ satellite peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the high-resolution Eu 3d spectra (Figure S8), the main peaks at binding energies of 1134.5 eV, 1164.5 eV in LD-Eu/Cu₂O... The high-resolution Cu 2p spectrum of Cu₂O (Figure 2a) delivers the main peaks of Cu2p₃/₂ and Cu2p₁/₂ at 932.2 and 952.2 eV

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu K-edge absorption lines decrease indicating reduced oxidation states; Eu L₃-edge main peak positive shift vs Eu₂O₃ confirming charge donation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2c shows the XANES spectra of the CuK-edge... demonstrating that the average oxidation states are reduced. The Eu L₃-edge absorption lines of LD-Eu/Cu₂O and HD-Eu/Cu₂O present a positive shift of the main peak relative to Eu₂O₃ (Figure 2d)

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu-O at 1.50 Å, Cu-Cu at 2.79 Å; CN_Cu-Cu 9.8 (LD-Eu/Cu₂O), 7.2 (HD-Eu/Cu₂O) vs 12 (Cu₂O); Eu-O at 1.99 Å dominant, no Eu-Eu signal in LD-Eu/Cu₂O.
nodes.evidence_snippet: both LD-Eu/Cu₂O and HD-Eu/Cu₂O exhibit Cu-O coordination at 1.50Å and Cu-O-Cu coordination at 2.79Å... Compared with the average Cu-Cu coordination number (CN_Cu-Cu) of 12 in Cu₂O, that in CN_Cu-Cu gradually decreases from 9.8 (LD-Eu/Cu₂O) to 7.2 (HD-Eu/Cu₂O)
